limited_overlap.description: 938 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 74,955 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
182 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10100 of 12000 applicants answered (84.2%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.57 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0013, causal_forest=-0.0014.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -8.3; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = 0.08. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = -6149 (90% -14952 to 2654).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = -85 (90% -908 to 738); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -7965, without months_unemployed = -143, without education = -241; full model = -147.
Run time 20 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10100.
